prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2015 – Summary (≤500 words)

Vision: Build a stronger economy and a fairer society with opportunity for everyone by 2020: balanced public finances, sustainable growth, high-quality public services, equal life chances, and decisive climate action.

Key pledges
- Balance the budget fairly by 2017/18; allow borrowing for productive investment.
- Cut taxes further by raising the Personal Allowance to £12,500.
- Invest £8bn a year more in the NHS by 2020 and guarantee parity for mental health.
- Protect education funding from nursery to age 19; qualified teachers in every class.
- Five Green Laws to protect nature, drive resource efficiency, green transport, zero-carbon power, and warmer homes.

Economy and finances
- Mixed approach to deficit reduction: no rises in headline Income Tax, NI, VAT or Corporation Tax; target the wealthy, banks, big business and polluters; clamp down on avoidance/evasion.
- Double economy-wide innovation/R&D; expand apprenticeships, National Colleges and regional growth funds; devolve economic powers locally.
- Reform business rates with a path to Land Value Tax; support SMEs, scale-ups and alternative finance.
- Green growth: expand Green Investment Bank, set a 2050 net-zero target and 2030 power decarbonisation, end unabated coal by 2025, boost storage, CCS, tidal and EVs; major energy efficiency programme.

Family finances, work and welfare
- More free childcare: towards 20 hours for ages 2–4 and from end of parental leave; complete Tax-Free Childcare; 85% childcare costs covered in Universal Credit.
- Universal Credit rollout with fair sanctions; devolved, tailored back-to-work support; protect young people’s safety net.
- Raise/strongly enforce Minimum Wage; promote Living Wage in public sector; transparency on gender pay and top-to-median pay ratios; fair flexible work and expanded Shared Parental Leave.
- Pensions: make the triple lock permanent; continue auto-enrolment; review single-rate tax relief.

Education and skills
- Protect early years, schools and 16–19 budgets; expand Pupil Premium; strengthen leadership and oversight; fair national funding formula; inclusive admissions.
- Parents’ Guarantee: qualified teachers and a slimmed core curriculum (including PSHE, consent, RE).
- Boost STEM and teacher development; expand apprenticeships (including higher/degree level); improve FE and university access, transparency and finance review.

Health and care
- NHS free at point of use; invest in community care, diagnostics and integration with social care; repeal forced-competition elements; protect the NHS from TTIP.
- Mental health: statutory waiting times, expand talking therapies, crisis care, perinatal and children’s services.
- Carers: £250 annual bonus, more rights and support; improve social care quality, workforce standards and end 15-minute visits.

Homes and energy
- Build 300,000 homes a year, 10+ Garden Cities, public land release, Housing Investment Bank.
- Affordable options: Rent to Own, shared ownership, Help to Rent deposit loans; stronger tenant protections and longer tenancies.
- Green Buildings Act: upgrade 4m homes by 2020; long-term EPC Band C target; council tax incentives; tougher PRS standards.

Rights, policing and justice
- Protect Human Rights Act; Digital Bill of Rights; a second Freedoms Act; oppose mass surveillance.
- Replace Police and Crime Commissioners with Police Boards; focus on prevention and rehabilitation; drug policy based on health (end imprisonment for possession for personal use).
- Tackle VAWG, FGM, and domestic abuse; stronger victims’ rights.

Devolution and democracy
- Home Rule within a federal UK; deliver Smith (Scotland), Silk (Wales) and Stormont agreements; English devolution on demand.
- Votes at 16; STV for Westminster and local elections; elected Lords; party funding reform with £10,000 cap.

Europe and world
- Remain in a reformed EU; complete the Single Market; support TTIP with NHS and standards safeguarded; in/out referendum only on future treaty change.
- Defence and security: single security budget; modern capabilities; reduce continuous nuclear patrols.
- Maintain 0.7% aid; lead on climate diplomacy; protect nature, oceans, and tackle illegal wildlife trade.
